$\frac{1+\sqrt2}{2+\sqrt3}$: multiply the numerator and denominator by $2-\sqrt3$, so the denominator becomes $4-3=1$:

$$(1+\sqrt2)(2-\sqrt3) = 2-\sqrt3+2\sqrt2-\sqrt6.$$

Group this as $2(1+\sqrt2)-(\sqrt3+\sqrt6)$, which has the required form with $A=2$, $B=2$, $C=3$, $D=6$.

(Swapping $C$ and $D$ gives the same sum.)

$A+B+C+D = 2+2+3+6 = 13$

ANSWER: 13
